Agents must reserve dedicated RAM matching active cryptographic proofs, functioning like a physical jetty anchoring each unique node to prevent sudden identity switching. Expanding an agent swarm beyond a tiny knoll triggers exponential hardware allocation costs, turning computation into a blazing comet of resource exhaustion. Attackers pay a compounding RAM rental fee per concurrent instance, making mass replication economically unviable while preserving access for single legitimate workers.
